rules.name: Literary Historical Sequence
rules.notes: Note: Students should take these courses prior to their senior year. If students need to take one or more of these classes after junior year, they should get permission in advance from their advisor or the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

rules.name: Methodology courses
rules.notes: Note: Students should take these courses prior to their senior year. If students need to take one or more of these classes after junior year, they should get permission in advance from their advisor or the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

rules.name: Literature (35 units)
rules.desc: 35 units of approved courses, only one of which may be a creative writing course, chosen from those offered by the Department of English. In place of one of these elective courses, students may choose one upper-division course in a foreign literature read in the original language. Courses must be taken for at least three units.

children.name: Capstone Seminar in English
children.desc:
The Capstone Seminar in English offers students the opportunity to revise a promising seminar paper or creative work from a previous class. The Capstone will combine the benefits of a workshop and an advanced seminar. Weekly readings will include texts in creative nonfiction, scholarly writing, and literary interpretation. Additionally, students will share their own work and provide constructive responses to other students. Students must email the instructor prior to the beginning of class with a copy of the work they plan to revise during the quarter. This capstone will be especially useful for those interested in preparing a strong writing sample for future applications, and for those who wished they had had more time to develop a previous, and still interesting, text.
The seminar is offered for three units.

children.name: Honors Program Capstone
children.desc:
The Honors Program in English provides another way for majors concentrating on literature to fulfill the capstone requirement. Students in the honors program participate in an honors seminar, perform individual research to develop an honors thesis in consultation with faculty and graduate-student advisors, and present their work at a public honors colloquium in the spring. Honors theses may be nominated for various awards within the department and the School of Humanities and Sciences.
Please see the Honors Requirement section below for further details.
children.notes: Note: English 196A should be taken for 5 units in the Autumn quarter and English 197 should be taken for 10 units (Senior Honors Essay) over the Winter and Spring quarters.

children.name: Creative Writing Capstone
children.desc: English majors concentrating in Creative Writing may fulfill the capstone requirement by completing a workshop in their area of specialty.

children.name: Interdisciplinary Studies Capstone
children.desc:
English majors concentrating in Interdisciplinary Studies who would like to complete a capstone project related to their area of concentration may present for approval to the Director of Undergraduate Studies a proposal for individual study in their senior year.
Unit count will vary depending on the project.

children.name: Computational Cultural Analytics Capstone
children.desc: Leveraging the unique resources of the Literary Lab, students will undertake their capstone project through a Lab course. Seniors in the track will be required to attend all meetings during the quarter that they take the course, as well as join a project and contribute to its research. Students may also choose to undertake their own research project within the Lab at the discretion of their advisor.

blocks.name: Honors

rules.name: Honors (optional)
rules.desc:
Students wishing to undertake a formal program of advanced literary criticism and scholarship, including the honors seminar and independent research, are invited to apply for the honors program in spring quarter of the junior year.
Admission is selective, and detailed requirements can be found on the English Department website.
Students are encouraged to participate in the Bing Honors College in September before their senior year. More information can be found on the department website.
rules.notes:
Enrollment Notes:

• course should be taken for 5 units in the Autumn quarter of the senior year, the senior-year seminar is designed to introduce students to the analysis and production of advanced literary scholarship. Students planning on studying abroad in their senior year should plan for winter quarter rather than autumn.

• course should be taken for 10 units (Senior Honors Essay) over the Winter and Spring quarters of the senior year under the supervision of a faculty advisor.

blocks.notes: Essays that receive a grade of A- or above are awarded honors.

rules.name: Subplan: Interdisciplinary Studies (40 units mimimum)
rules.desc: This program is intended for students who wish to combine the study of one broadly defined literary topic, period, genre, theme, or problem with an interdisciplinary program of courses (generally chosen from one other discipline) relevant to that inquiry.

children.name: Elective Literature Courses
children.desc: Twenty-five units of elective literature courses chosen from among those offered by the Department of English. Students must select two of these courses in relation to their interdisciplinary focus.

children.name: Interdisciplinary Courses
children.desc: Fifteen units related to the area of inquiry. These courses may be chosen from another department or interdisciplinary program within the School of Humanities and Sciences; they must form a cohesive study program to your selected literature courses and must be pre-approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

rules.name: Subplan: Creative Writing ( 40 units minimum)
rules.desc: This program is designed for students who want a sound basic knowledge of the English literary tradition as a whole and, at the same time, want to develop skills in writing poetry or prose. In addition to the degree requirements required of all majors listed above, students must complete at least 40 additional units of approved courses in either the prose or poetry concentration.

children.name: Prose Elective Requirements
children.desc: Elective courses must be taken for at least 3 units, and the total number of courses must equal 20 units. (One of the courses may be fulfilled with a creative writing workshop).

children.name: Poetry Elective Requirements
children.desc: Elective courses must be taken for at least three units, and the total number of courses must equal 20 units. (One of the courses may be fulfilled with a creative writing workshop)

rules.name: Subplan: Literature and Philosophy (40-50 units)
rules.desc: Students should meet with the undergraduate director concerning the Literature and Philosophy focus. This track is for students who wish to explore interdisciplinary studies at the intersection of literature and philosophy while acquiring knowledge of the English language literary tradition as a whole.

children.name: Gateway Courses
children.notes:
NOTE: PHIL 80 requires a prerequisite philosophy course (not including PHIL99), that may require an additional 3-5 units of coursework.
It is advised that ENGLISH 81 be taken as early as possible in the student's career, normally in the sophomore year.

children.name: Electives and Capstone
children.desc:
• Two upper division courses of special relevance to the study of Philosophy and Literature. Both of these courses must be in the English department. A list of approved courses is available on this Philosophy and Literature website.

• Two additional elective courses in the English department.

• One capstone seminar course of relevance to the study of Philosophy and Literature. A list of approved courses is available on this Philosophy and Literature website.

rules.name: Subplan: Computational Cultural Analytics ( 41 units minimum)
rules.desc: This program is designed for students interested in combining the study of English literary history and theory with the use and study of contemporary methods and concepts of data science, computation and statistics. Students will take courses in data science and relevant English department elective courses chosen in consultation with their advisor.

children.name: Electives (18-20 Units)
children.desc:
Elective units must be from the English Department.
Elective courses must be taken for at least three units, and the total number of courses must equal 20 units. These units may be taken as Literature or Creative Writing courses. Students may substitute ONE course for a relevant class taught elsewhere in the University, in consultation with your advisor.
